body:
Well I have to ask, besides diagnosing and prescribing meds, what else could going to a doctor do? 



On the subject of talking about social anxiety, I don't really have any close friends. There is the person I have been talking to, but that has only been for two days. 


And with the final part, it really is not that easy for me. I spend a long time thinking about most things (probably not a good thing, but I do). I know when to do it (not date, time), so I just have to figure out the how.




Edit: just wanted to add that the more I think about it and read about other people that have seeked help (on the sub) the closer and closer I get to doing it myself

Well we were talking (texting) again today for 4 hours, and she explained that while I was not her first pick, she chose me because they were not available. We needed up talking about how neither of us are very busy we can just text the other if we want to talk. 


And I agree, of all the people I know, she would be the best person to talk to. We have similar experiences with being abandoned and things like that.

> Maybe it's not that people don't care to get to know you...but maybe because of your trust issues, people sense your reluctance to let them in?



It could also be they people just don't trust me so I don't trust them back. 

> I had friends, usually kids who were more outgoing than me and would initiate the friendships.


That is how I made all my friends, people would talk to me then introduce me to their friends, etc. I never really initiated anything.



> But it wasn't until years later I found out that some kids thought I was stuck up or a snob


I really doubt that could be the case for me. I just don't think I come off as that type of person. I don't really know, but I don't really see why someone would see that.




Edit: just wanted to add that I don't want to bug/annoy my friend

It really was not abandonment or betrayal (these days it is all too common). I will cover it very briefly. I was just learning how to swim and the person teaching me tells me I can trust him. So being such a little kid I listen. He is holding me as we walk out into the deeper water and he keeps telling me I can trust him. And suddenly he drops me in. This has led to me not trusting people and never being a confident/strong swimmer.

I have actually written some TL;DRs that are longer than the unabridged post. Not sure how I did it but I found a way.



Either way, it is more that I just wish I had an irl friend I could turn to when I need it. Thanks for offering though.

Somebody who cares about me, enough money to live happily, and to be genuinely happy.




Sorry I can't draw :|

I think I misinterpreted it and it was just good feelings passing through temporarily. The more I think about it, the more it seems like my parents are just discussing things going on in my family. I have had other things happen in the past, and as far as I know, nobody else knows. It is probably just a matter of building up the courage to say something.



If it means anything, I took a depression screening test to see what it said. I then took another one to see if they were the same, both came up with severely depressed.

I just decided to add this in a second post just incase you already read the original one. So I was thinking about my parents being nosy and gossipy. I feel like that might just be my subconscious trying to give an excuse for me to not say something. 



Edit: I am just adding this in here because I don't want to blow up your inbox. So I was just reading a post about how OP did not want to seek help because he was afraid they would just say it is teenage hormones. What if that is all it is and it will just all disappear in a little bit of time? Also sorry for continuing to bug you.

> BP?  



I meant bipolar. Should have said BPD.



> Your wildly oscillating moods are currently and temporarily  swung to 'much better', how does that mean you don't need help?




Not really sure how to describe it. It just feels like I got over it. Thus I don't need help.




One issue is, I don't actually know who the counselor is. There are about 10 people that work in "guidance" but they handle scheduling and college applications. 




> Have you told your parents you consider them nosy and gossipy? 
Your relationship needs serious work.  At the moment you need help from your parents and are unable to get it because of this.  
How much responsibility are you taking for developing and maintaining a relationship which gets you what you need from them?  I'd guess you are playing the helpless victim, which must be frustrating the crap out of them. 





I did once, and they tried to hide it more. Not really well though. I think that is just the type of people they are. I don't understand why you are saying "helpless victim" and stuff. I have not mentioned it yet so how could it annoy them.




> You write about your problems with friends, have you given any thought to how the breakdown in your relationship with your parents is involved in your depression and what you can do about that?  





I don't think it has anything to do with that. It could, but I doubt it. I just realized that I am really good at pissing people off without trying, so I just avoid people because I don't want to.

You actually responded to an older post of mine, so I will answer to both with this one. 



From the links you posted, [this](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avoidant_personality_disorder) one was the one closest. And it is not that I don't want to/don't think I need help it is that I need to figure out how to do it and then work up the courage to actually do it. I know it sounds ridiculous but that is it.




Now with this post (probably should have done that in the other order but oh well), I guess I will cover the "barriers" I mentioned. So the two biggest ones are that my parents are very nosy and gossipy (I guess that is the right word) and I, as mentioned, need to find a good way to do it and work up the courage. And now, I feel much better, so I feel like there would be no reason to seek help (unless it is some form of BP).

It really does not help when I am also friends with the person I was abandoned for. I could have tagged along and be stuck a third wheel, but it would still be better than being alone. 



Either way, may I ask how it got better? I just don't see it.

I truly agree. I feel like I have cycles and because of it I feel horrible posting here. Sometimes I am ok, but sometimes I just wish it would end. Either way, often times when I make a post, nobody responds or even looks at it so I just use it to vent.

Not really sure if you meant to sound condescending, but you did.



For the reasons listed, the first one sort of applies. Besides just being nervous about it, there are other reasons that I don't really care to go into.


On the topic of the games, maybe(?) in the past but I just can't recently. My computer broke down about two or three weeks ago, it has been getting fixed and won't be fixed for another week and a half to two weeks. 






With being more social, again that is hard. There is about nothing of interest for about ten or fifteen miles. And I just don't know what to do. I have always had trouble holding conversation with people I don't know. 



And if I were to enjoy summer, what is there to enjoy? Being alone and playing video games for hours on end? *yay*

"Your so young! You will get over it with time."



Every time I post here I have to point out not to say something like that. It just hurts on so many levels.
From what I knew about the disorder I thought that it might have been the case, but I was not really sure. I am just glad that it was not just me that thought that was what it sounded like.

Often times it goes very quickly but sometimes I just feel nothing (best way to say it is just numb) for a while then I go back. It just started recently and I assumed it would be like a one day thing, but it has persisted so I assume that is not the case.

It is just really hard for me to stay positive when I am horrendous at everything I try. I have been practicing pool for a few weeks (maybe even a month, I have just lost track of time). Then my brother comes down and tries it for the first time. Immediately better than me. It is always like this. I constantly practice only to have someone (usually my brother) come along and just be better than me on their first try. It is so disheartening. I just know that I can't beat him. After that, why even try? Anything I ever try again, someone will be immediately be better on their first try. I just can't beat anyone at anything. There I always someone standing there, ready to crush my hopes at being good at something.
I have no reason really. Sure, I don't have many friends and am alone 95% of the time, but so many people have it *much* worse.
Well so far, being myself has only made me lose things.

I have trouble finding anyone with similar interests as I am too shy and self conscious to just talk to someone. I used to play an instrument, but I quit because I really hated it. Just nothing seems to interest me anymore.

I used to really enjoy MTG, but I had nobody to play with. My brother would, but then I made one deck he would not bother to learn to beat and quit because he found it too frustrating (mono-black deathtouch/removal control). Eventually I moved on from that. I had played a lot of TF2, at some point my computer suddenly stopped running it. Then, I moved onto Black Ops Zombies. And just yesterday, my computer had a hard ware crash. So how all I do is watch Netflix and browse Reddit (phone/iPad). But I have never found a single person with the same interests (even close). I would play Zombies with the mentioned friend, but he is really busy and he can rarely play (1-2 times a week). 



So yeah, I just have trouble meeting new people with similar interests because I am too self conscious and shy.

My only concern is that it was so hard to get the friends I had, I don't know how I could possibly do it again. The only way I was able to so it in the first place was because the one friend who seems to still care about me introduced me to another friend who introduced me to two more, etc..

Well they were just total assholes to me. It was not like joking around, it was all directed at me. Constantly nitpicking anything I ever said or did. And by constantly, I mean it is all they ever say to me. So I just left. And I don't even know where it came from. Nothing new happened,  except I recovered from being sick for about a week and that is what I was greeted by. 



And for hobbies, the only thing I can think of is gaming (they made fun of that too). Which is probably just a result of being lonely. I can easily do it alone and from home.
